newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of March 17, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Digital Equipment Corp is on the verge of a management shakeup that could mean greater authority for Bruce Claflin, a vice president and general manager of its PC business, PC Week reported March 17. Sources told PC Week that Claflin is in line to assume post of president or chief operating officer. The moves could happen this week.

Compaq Computer Corp will introduce next month at its Innovate Forum 97 conference two Armada notebook PCs, one which is code-named StarTrek with a 166 megahertz Pentium chip, MMX technology and a 13.3 inch thin-film display, PC Week reported March 17.

COMPUTERWORLD - Microsoft Corp said its next major release of its Office suite of applications will offer a server-based solution for users implementing a network computer strategy based on Microsoft's NetPC specification, Computerworld reported March 17.
IBM next month plans to upgrade its line of mainframe disk arrays on April 8 to give users more than a good price when choosing storage options, Computerworld reported March 17.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Compaq Computer Corp CEO Eckhard Pfeiffer told computer reseller executives last week that Compaq will engage in a joint manufacturing program with the channel by midyear. Compaq also plans to pursue an internal manufacturing plan to do some build-to-order and configuations for small and midsized businesses, CRN reported March 17.

IBM Corp will install 10,000 of its own network computers inside the company during 1997, in one of the largest corporate adoption plans for the NC, showing IBM's commitment to the product, CRN reported March 17.
INFOWORLD - Intel Corp, Microsoft Corp and Compaq plan to launch a specification to support clustering, competing with a similar effort by Sun Microsystems Inc, InfoWorld reported March 17.
Sun and International Business Machines Corp plan to announce April 2 they will standardize on Java Beans rather than OpenDoc as their enterprise object model, InfoWorld said.
INFORMATION WEEK - It appears likely that Netscape Communications Corp and Microsoft soon will dominate much of the emerging market in push technology, Information Week reported March 17.

Revlon's plans to migrate from mainframe-based applications to SAP AG's R/3 is far behind schedule and over budget, Information Week reported, citing unidentified sources. Problems are being blamed on the difficulty of implementing the system on IBM's SP platform.

EE TIMES - Microsoft Corp announced plans at last week's embedded systems conference with its plans to broaden the market base of its Windows CE operating system beyond Personal Digital Assistants, EE Times reported March 17.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS NEWS - The announcement last week by LG Semicon Co Ltd that its 64-bit DRAM technology has been adapted to a 0.35 micron standard-cell ASIC process underscores the extensive moves made by South Korean chip makers to shift a major portion of their business to nonmemory devices by 2000, EE Times reported March 17

PC OEMs are rewriting the rules of system design to meet requirements of the sub-$1,000 box, as market acceptance over the past year has shattered the myth that customers only desire the latest in PC technology, EBN reported March 17.

MAC WEEK - Four more division heads resigned from Apple last week, Dale Fuller, head of PowerBooks, Maury Austin, imaging chief, H.L. Cheung, previously in charge of consumer Macs, and Mike Dionne, leader of customer assistance, MacWeek reported March 17.
